clue.text: Interrogator about to request main first suspects to come in

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of 'to request main' are rearranged
first asks for the opening letter of the word suspects, which joins the mix

explanation.surface: A detective's interrogator asks the main suspects to come in for questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles TO REQUEST MAIN, and 'first suspects' adds S; 'to come in' says that S joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The host of a quiz show interrogates contestants, putting questions to them, hence an interrogator.

clue.text: They go without saying to get estimate to large retailer

parts.note: a quotation is a builder's price estimate
Marks, short for Marks & Spencer, a big British high-street chain store

explanation.surface: Some things are so obvious they need no saying, like getting a price from a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: these punctuation marks sit outside what is said. Marks & Spencer is a major British department store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas enclose spoken words, standing outside the saying itself; a witty definition.

clue.text: Nurses near being manipulated into trap

parts.note: ENs are Enrolled Nurses, a grade of British nurse

indicators.note: manipulated means worked by hand into a new shape, so the letters of near are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nurses nearby are being manoeuvred into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like a verb but gives Enrolled Nurses, a British nursing grade; 'into' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a snare is to trap; the verb and the clue word are synonyms.

clue.text: Elephantine facility needed an operator's assistance

definitions.meaning: humorously, the cry an elephant makes through its trunk
a long-distance phone call that in the old days had to be connected by an operator

explanation.surface: Something elephant-sized required help from someone at a switchboard.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUNK CALL is the old British term for a long-distance telephone call, which once had to go through an operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-distance calls went over trunk lines and needed a switchboard operator; an elephant calls with its trunk.

clue.text: Unequal match so denied surprising result

indicators.note: a surprising result is one turned upside down, so the letters of 'so denied' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lopsided contest is refused, which turns out to be an unexpected outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A lopsided contest where one side dominates is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Insect might get up in the air

parts.note: may and might both express possibility
to fly is to rise up into the air

explanation.surface: An insect could take off into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-lived winged creature is a well-known kind of insect, hatching in spring.

clue.text: Indian's term of respect starts straight after he is born

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: An Indian honorific is used right from the moment a boy is born.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India this was the polite form of address for a European man, a title of respect.

clue.text: Witticism coming three times from George Orwell's farm animals

parts.words: coming three times from George Orwell's
parts.note: the letter E is the one that appears three times in the name George Orwell
a pig is a farm animal
a ram, a male sheep, is another farm animal

explanation.surface: A clever saying repeated three times by the animals in Orwell's novel Animal Farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the slogans of Animal Farm, but the phrase points to a letter: George Orwell contains E three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, pointed, clever saying is an epigrammatic witticism; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: A dental surgery's role as gas supplier?

definitions.text: A dental surgery's role as gas supplier?

parts.words: A dental surgery's role as gas supplier
parts.note: a dentist's surgery is where teeth get fillings, and it also gives gas as anaesthetic; a petrol station supplies gas

explanation.surface: A dentist's practice doubles as a place to buy gas.
explanation.walkthrough: In American English gas is petrol, sold at a roadside forecourt; a dentist puts fillings in teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside fuel forecourt goes by this name; read literally, it is a place where tooth cavities get filled.

clue.text: Obsolete remedy has laboratory extremely in the dark

parts.note: OBS is the dictionary abbreviation for obsolete
a cure is a remedy

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word laboratory

explanation.surface: An out-of-date treatment is being developed in a lab under conditions of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in an unclear or hidden way, as if in darkness; the adverb fits the phrase.

clue.text: Greeting covers small island in the Caribbean

indicators.note: covers means one word goes around another, wrapping it

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: A welcome sign hangs over a little island in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' looks like the definition, but it belongs to AIT; the definition is just where the country lies.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic occupies the western part of the island of Hispaniola, in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Black beginning with a word of regret

indicators.note: beginning with a says the word black should start with the letter a instead of its own first letter

explanation.surface: Starting with a black mark is something to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, as in 'alas and alack'.

clue.text: Intolerant one left party

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the Liberal Party is a British political party

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded person has quit a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow-minded and unwilling to accept others' views; the opposite of broad-minded.

clue.text: Repeats treatise after readjustment

indicators.note: readjustment means set in a new order, so the letters of treatise are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone restates an academic treatise once it has been revised.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do something again is to repeat it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: 1 across peace when war in the Far East is over

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace

indicators.note: is over means the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: 'Nam is slang for the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: Peace finally arrives once fighting in Asia has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is QUESTION MASTER: Jeremy Paxman hosted the British TV quiz University Challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: This British broadcaster was for decades the host of the student quiz University Challenge.

clue.text: Longing for a quiet canoodle in French country surroundings

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to pet is to kiss and cuddle
en is French for in

indicators.note: surroundings asks for the outer letters of the word country

explanation.surface: A yearning to cuddle quietly somewhere in rural France.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for a craving or strong desire, so a synonym for longing.

clue.text: Artistic sect's mural a non-starter

parts.note: a cult is a sect

indicators.note: a non-starter means the word mural loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sect's wall painting turns out to be a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the arts and culture; artistic in a broad sense.

clue.text: Cosy up to large food and drink company

definitions.meaning: ...é, the Swiss multinational behind many coffee and chocolate brands

explanation.surface: Getting friendly with a big food and drinks firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuggle against someone; also the name of the Swiss food giant.

clue.text: Boss getting to eat out more

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper

indicators.note: out signals the letters of more are put out of order

explanation.surface: The boss gets to dine out more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eat out' looks like a phrase about restaurants, but 'out' is the signal working on 'more' alone; 'getting to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for the person in overall charge; a chief or boss.

clue.text: 1 across carries a heavy load over a period of time at the beginning of the year

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece is placed over the others

parts.note: to hump is to lug something heavy
HR is the abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: at the beginning of asks for the first letter of the word year

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a heavy burden for a while at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is QUESTION MASTER: John Humphrys hosted the British TV quiz Mastermind.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh broadcaster was host of the BBC quiz programme Mastermind from 2003.

clue.text: Supplementary tax somehow to be deducted from expiration otherwise

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of tax are not removed in the order they are written
deducted from says the letters of tax are taken out of expiration
otherwise means arranged in another way, so what is left of expiration is reordered

explanation.surface: A supplementary tax is somehow subtracted when something expires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be deducted from' takes T, A, X ('somehow' in any order) out of EXPIRATION; 'otherwise' rearranges EPIRION.
explanation.definitionFit: In baroque music, ripieno parts are the supplementary players who fill out the full orchestra.

clue.text: It produces purge of fool employed in big agency

indicators.note: employed in means placed inside an organisation, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: the CIA is the American Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool on the payroll of a large agency triggers a clean-out of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purge' suggests a political clean-out but means a laxative: senna pods come from a kind of cassia.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassia plant yields senna, a traditional laxative, so it produces a purge.

clue.text: Candidate to plan pact reforms with independent in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre says one letter goes into the middle of the rearranged letters
reforms means shapes again, so the letters of 'plan pact' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political candidate plans to reform a pact with an independent in the middle ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges PLAN PACT to APPLCANT, and I goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone applying for a post or position is a candidate for it.

clue.text: Playwright in the same place makes a lot of sense

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place, used in references

indicators.note: a lot of means most, but not all, of the word sense

explanation.surface: A playwright's work in one place makes good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Indian music he tries to eavesdrop in recital

indicators.note: in recital means when spoken out, so we go by sound

parts.note: a tapper is someone who taps phones to listen in

explanation.surface: An Indian music performer tries to overhear a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech TAPPER and TAPPA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappa is a form of Indian semi-classical vocal music from the Punjab.

clue.text: Walks unsteadily on boats

definitions.meaning: to keel is to lurch or totter, as in keeling over
a keel is a flat-bottomed boat used to carry coal on the Tyne

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Keel can mean to stagger or roll over; it is also a flat-bottomed coal barge of north-east England.

clue.text: It's plain to see I get sneer anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any order, so the letters of 'I get sneer' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is obvious, though I get mocked regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like 'obvious', but it is grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania, famous for its wildlife migration.

clue.text: Rely on job at ranch to be drunk on hard liquor

indicators.note: being drunk is being in a muddled state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Relying on a ranch job, someone ends up drunk on spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the folk personification of barley and the alcoholic drink made from it, especially whisky.
